text: What if I told you La Llorona's legend is far older than the story of a mother drowning her children?
Centuries ago, the people of ancient Mexico told of a mysterious woman crying through the darkness.
Before the Spanish conquest, an omen described a woman wandering the streets, desperately crying out for her children.
Some researchers connect those cries to Cihuacóatl, an ancient Aztec goddess associated with motherhood.
Over time, another story emerged. A woman named María, betrayed by the man she loved, drowned her own children in a river.
Consumed by guilt and sorrow, her spirit was said to wander the rivers forever, screaming: ¡Ay, mis hijos!
But historians have never confirmed that this tragedy happened. Different regions tell completely different versions of her story.
Maybe La Llorona was never one woman. But for centuries, one terrifying warning has survived: never follow the crying near the water.
